known_stress_episodes.label: GFC oil-demand collapse
known_stress_episodes.note: Petroleum stocks rose sharply as demand weakened into recession.

known_stress_episodes.label: COVID demand shock
known_stress_episodes.note: Inventories rose during the abrupt collapse in mobility and fuel demand.

mechanism: Hypothesis, not established fact: when petroleum inventories build alongside stable or expanding production rather than pure demand collapse, the build can signal robust supply availability and softer energy-price pressure. That combination may support consumer spending and corporate margins over the following 6-12 months, which is consistent with the procyclical quartile gradient and the searched Long/Cash winner.
caveats: Fragile evidence: the selected rule was found in a broad search, not confirmed by a final holdout exam.
Bootstrap p=0.099 is not significant at the 5% level; confidence is low.
Granger significance clusters at 6-8 months while the tournament-selected rule uses L12, so the lead range is imprecise.
The overlay lowers drawdown but gives up annualized return versus buy-and-hold.
narrative_summary: Total petroleum stocks overturn the natural counter-cyclical prior in this sample: Q1 lowest 3-month inventory growth has Sharpe 0.37 and 6.0% annualized return, while Q4 highest has Sharpe 1.25 and 17.5%, and the winner is procyclical Long/Cash at L12. Treat the result as a low-confidence defensive overlay within a 6-12 month lead band.
key_finding: Petroleum inventories provide a weak, empirically mixed equity signal. Winner is petrol_level_z60 / T2_roll_p25 / P1_long_cash (pro) / L11 / LB36 with OOS Sharpe 1.53 vs buy-and-hold 0.93; max drawdown -7.6% vs -23.9%. Toda-Yamamoto Granger indicator->SPY significant lags: [6, 7, 8]; SPY->indicator significant lags: none. Treat as a searched defensive overlay, not established causal alpha.
